title: Coco Gauff says an ‘insane’ wave of racist abuse followed a disputed point at China Open | CNN
text:
Source: AP

Coco Gauffsaid she received an “insane” amount of racist comments on social media following a controversial point in her China Openmatchagainst home player Sun Xinran.

Gauff stopped a rally after electronic advertising boards lining the court flickered during a point late in the first set of her 7-5, 6-1 third-round victory over Sun, a 16-year-old who recently won theUS Openjunior title.

“Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist,” Gauff, who is Black, said ina reply on X. “The amount of racist comments/dms I’ve received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I’m not a cheater or a thief.”

Sun appeared about to win the point when Gauff stopped playing. The chair umpire then ordered the point to be replayed.

Gauff, a two-time grand slam champion ranked No. 4, went on to take control of the match on Monday.

“Xinran is (an) incredible talent and player, I apologized for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood,”Gauff added in another post.

Sun, who was given a wild card entry by tournament organizers and was making her WTA Tour debut, appeared distraught after the loss.

Gauff, who reached the fourth round of Wimbledon as a 15 year old in 2019, sympathized with Sun.

“I did not like to see her so emotional as I’ve been there and I really understand what it is like, but this is just the beginning of an incredible career,” Gauff said. “It was an honor to share the court in front of her home crowd.”
